identity_and_inventory.finding: EO10014 is the single unnumbered continuing direction to heads of executive departments, agencies, and independent establishments to take practicable action, with State and local pollution authorities, so disposal of federal wastes and regulator-destroyed products conforms with applicable State programs. Both waste categories are parts of the same command, not unexamined independent exceptions. There are no separate reporting, implementation, fixed-sunset, contingent-end, or one-time transfer commands.

first_ending.reason: The original is a recurring rule for waste disposal, so compliance with one disposal or cooperation episode does not exhaust it. It contains no own-term sunset or report-triggered end. No earlier named amendment/termination was found in the bounded later-event catalog or independent searches. The express whole-order supersession in section9 is the first located effective cessation. Statutory changes in water-pollution policy do not themselves state a sunset for this presidential direction; no contrary named instrument was found. The owner unnamed-instrument ruling remains controlling; this is not an amendment-as-first-end theory.

savings.reason: No savings of EO10014 operative commands appears in its complete text or any part of EO11258. Similar successor pollution-control duties arise under EO11258 and independent law; they do not keep the superseded order operative. Historical conduct and possible accrued rights/liabilities are not erased by this conclusion. The observed Starrett and Aragon litigation invokes historical pollution conduct: Starrett expressly did not decide EO10014 because EO11258 sufficed; Aragon interprets practicability in the historical command and dismisses the FTCA action under the discretionary-function exception. Neither read judgment reinstates10014 or saves an ongoing10014 command. This finding is confined to residual operative force; it is not an adjudication extinguishing all accrued tort or cleanup liabilities.
